Abstract

Paul, 18 November 2026: "do a lab report about the maintenance, the visualization techniques. Do a lab report on the thermal regulation features of orrery fleet management. Start with a how to use guide. Show pictures, annotate them and give descriptions ... Starting as a HOW TO guide, with scientific and formulas showing and some sample calculations."

A fleet of eight computers heats an apartment whose own heating is switched off. Since 16:44 on 17 November Orrery holds the room that the fleet stands in at 80 °F by itself: every five minutes it reads two thermometers in the room and the weather at the airport, works out how many watts the room wants moved, and takes one step, a lane of work paused or resumed, or a whole machine finished, powered off and later woken by a network packet.

Part One of this report is how to use it: where the panels are, what each control does, and the orders a person can give. Part Two is the science: the one heat balance everything is worked from, with seven calculations done on the fleet's own numbers. Part Three is what the first fifteen hours showed. The room was held between 78.1 and 81.3 °F, with one excursion to about 81.6 °F at 18:44 that a person had to end; eight faults in the law were found and seven were corrected the same day. Part Four is how the heat is drawn, and why. Part Five is its upkeep.

The house's loss per degree is still not measured. The figure in use, 120 W/°C, is a working value, and everything that rests on it says so.

I. The questions

  1. How does a person use it: set a temperature, see what it is doing, take a machine in hand?
  2. What is it calculating, and can each number be checked by hand?
  3. Did it hold the room, and where did it fail?
  4. How is the heat shown, and what does each mark on the screen mean?
  5. What does it need from a person, daily and weekly?

Part One: how to use it

II. The five-minute guide

Where. In Orrery: Queue, then Heat in the left column. The Heat page has six panels in a row of chips; the first two are the ones for this.

PanelWhat it is for
HearthThe controls: the target, the mode, the power buttons, and the controller's own account of what it is doing
DiagramThe picture: where the heat comes from, where it goes, and the thermometers

To set the temperature. On the Hearth panel press − 0.5 or + 0.5, or type a number in the field and press Return. The field takes 26.7, 26.7 C or 80 F.

To switch regulation on or off. Three mode buttons:

ModeWhat happens
offNothing is read and nothing is done
adviseEvery five minutes it works everything out and says what it would do. It changes no machine
actIt does it. The button is framed in red and must be pressed twice

To take a machine in hand. The power row has a cell for each machine and one button: On (send the wake packet; when the machine answers it is put to work) or Off (press twice; the machine finishes its job, leaves the queue and is powered off). The machine that carries the room's thermometers has no Off.

To see why it did something. The hold line says the budget in watts and the last thing it said. The whole record is one file, a line a look: QUEUE/hearth/hold.log.

If the room is too warm right now. Lower the target by a degree. That sheds heat at the next pass. If the room is at the ceiling, the controller sheds without waiting. A door opened is faster than either.

To stop it and take over. Press advise. Lanes it paused stay paused until you resume them or set act again.

III. The Hearth panel, mark by mark

MarkWhat it isHow to read it
1The target, in both scalesThe temperature being held. Here 26.7 °C, 80.1 °F
2Changing itHalf a degree down, half a degree up, or a number typed and Return
3The modeThe one in force is underlined. act is red-framed and asks twice
4The power switchWhether act may power machines off and wake them. It has no button: tools/hearth.py QUEUE set power on or off
5The holdThe law in force, its budget in watts, the room and its slope, the ceiling, the lanes it holds paused, and its last words
6The power rowA cell a machine: what it is doing, whether it is known to wake by the packet, and its On or Off button
7The plan's ageWhen the controller last looked. Over fifteen minutes old, something has stopped
8The room and its probesEach thermometer, where it is, what it reads, how old the reading is, and whether it is believed
9The balanceGreen: the watts the fleet draws now. The mark: the watts wanted. Under it, the budget's own arithmetic
10The ladderThe older law's list of steps, shown for comparison. It does not act while the law is hold

The red paragraph under the mode buttons says, in words, exactly what act will do with the power switch as it stands. Read it before pressing act.

IV. The Diagram panel, mark by mark

MarkWhat it isHow to read it
1The weatherThe outer frame is the outside air. The reading is the airport's, with its age
2The wallsThe hatched band round the apartment. The heat that leaves crosses it
3Zone 1, the fleet's roomThe room the thermometers are in, its temperature, and how far it is from the target
4The machinesA tile each: watts now as a bar and a number; the CPU's temperature and time constant (tau); the drives' temperature and lag; how many drives and sensors report. A dim tile is a machine that is off
5The collectorEvery machine's heat runs to this bar. A pipe's thickness is its watts
6HEAT INThe fleet's total watts: the heat going into the room. JI is a power reading
7Heat in, six hoursThe same number as a trend
8The air and the thermal massA tank. It says SOAKING UP when the room is warming (heat going into walls, floor and furniture), GIVING BACK when it is cooling, HOLDING when it is still. The level is the room's temperature between 60 and 90 °F
9The room, three hoursThe room's trend, with the target (green dots) and the ceiling (red dots)
10Other heatEverything that warms the room and is not the fleet. It is implied, not read
11Zone 2, the rest of the apartmentDrawn in dashes with an empty TI bubble: there is no thermometer there
12THROUGH THE WALLSThe watts leaving to the weather. The line under it says which figure it rests on
13The thermometersThe room, with its target and ceiling marked, and the weather, on one scale; every probe listed under them
14The balanceIn equals out, in one line, with the equation

The numbers are the controller's plan, so they change at each pass, about every five minutes. The bright marks in the pipes move continuously, in the direction the heat flows.

V. The command line

QUEUE is the queue's directory. Everything a button does, and the few things no button does:

CommandWhat it does
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE statusOne screen: the room, the plan, what it would do. Changes nothing
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE target 26.7The target, in °C
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE mode off / advise / actThe mode
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE set ceiling 27.2The temperature the room must not stand above, °C
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE set power on / offWhether act may power machines off and wake them
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE set law hold / ladderWhich law acts
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE set ua 120The house's loss per degree, when it is measured
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE power-off NAME / power-on NAMEOne machine, by hand
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE machine NAME wol on / offWhether a machine is known to wake by the packet
python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE probesEvery thermometer and what it reads
python3 tools/hearth-energy.py QUEUEEach machine's joules and what it did for them
python3 tools/hearth-house.py QUEUE --tableThe house's fit so far; also saves the week's weather
tail -f QUEUE/hearth/hold.logWhat the controller is saying, as it says it

VI. Making a machine switchable

A machine is powered off by the controller only if it is known to come back. To prove one:

  1. With it on, arm its network card (root, your password): scp tools/fleet-wol.sh user@NAME: && ssh -t user@NAME 'doas sh fleet-wol.sh on'
  2. Press Off twice on its cell. Wait until it is down.
  3. Press On. A server board tests its memory first; allow some minutes.
  4. If it answers, it is marked as waking by the packet and the controller may switch it from then on.
MachineWakes by the packetSeconds to answer
calberyes, with no recipe needed32, 52
bosporusyes, after the recipe112 to 286 (one of 602)
jaguaribeyesabout 120
boburner, whitewolfuntried: their only cable is in a 10 GbE card
columbiauntried: card not armed
saskatchewannever switched off: it carries the thermometers

Part Two: the science

VII. One balance

The room is treated as one lump of heat:

C dT/dt = P + P0 − UA (T − To) (1)

SymbolMeaningUnitWhere it comes from
Tthe room°Ctwo thermometers, read every five seconds
Tothe weather°Cthe airport's observation
Pthe fleet's watts at the wallWeach machine's energy counter and card; a model where there is none
dT/dtthe room's slope°C/ha line through the last hour's looks
Cthe joules that warm the room one degreeJ/°Cmeasured: 4.2 MJ/°C, by the step of 17 November
UAwatts lost for each degree over the weatherW/°Cnot measured: 120 is in use
P0every watt that is not the fleet'sWnot measured: what is left over

Three things follow from (1), and the screen draws all three.

Where the room settles. With dT/dt = 0:

T_ss = To + (P + P0) / UA (2)

How fast it gets there.

τ = C / UA (3)

The three flows on the Diagram.

through the walls = UA (T − To) (4) soak = C dT/dt (5) other heat = walls + soak − P (6)

VIII. The budget

The controller does not use gains. It asks how many watts would have to be added or taken away for the room to stop where it is wanted:

budget = −( UA (T − target) + C dT/dt ) (7)

The first term is what the walls will lose more or less of once the room is at the target. The second is what the room is storing or giving up as it moves now; stopping the movement means taking that away. The budget is held within 600 W either way, because a thermometer that reads in tenths cannot justify more.

Then one step: the first, in the order of preference, whose watts are no more than twice the budget.

PreferenceRule
1. Graphics machines are keptHeat is shed from a machine without a card before one with, and from a CPU lane before a card's lane. Heat is added the other way about
2. Work for the jouleAmong equals, the machine that spends most energy on a job goes first and comes back last
At the ceilingThe preference gives way: the largest step that is no more than twice the budget

And the pace: forty minutes between changes, because the room answers about an hour late; fifteen when the budget is 400 W or more; ten at the ceiling.

IX. Seven calculations, on the fleet's own numbers

Each can be checked against hold.log or the picture it came from.

1. A budget, on a quiet morning. 06:37, 18 November: room 26.00 °C, target 26.7, slope −0.07 °C/h.

UA term: 120 × (26.00 − 26.7) = −84 W C term: 4.2×10⁶ × (−0.07) / 3600 = −82 W budget: −(−84 − 82) = +166 W (the log says +164)

The room wants 166 W more. Every machine was already on, so nothing was done.

2. A budget at its limit. 18:37, 17 November: room 27.10 °C, slope +0.69 °C/h.

UA term: 120 × (27.10 − 26.7) = +48 W C term: 4.2×10⁶ × 0.69 / 3600 = +805 W budget: −(48 + 805) = −853 W, held at −600 W

Nearly all of it is the second term: the room was not far over its target, it was rising fast. This is why a law that looked only at the error would have done almost nothing.

3. The three flows on the Diagram. 08:21, 18 November (the picture in section IV): fleet 1,209 W, room 26.8 °C, weather 11.0 °C, slope +0.60 °C/h.

through the walls: 120 × (26.8 − 11.0) = 1,896 W soak: 4.2×10⁶ × 0.60 / 3600 = 700 W (drawn: 702) other heat: 1,896 + 700 − 1,209 = 1,387 W (drawn: 1,389)

4. The room's time constant. By (3):

τ = 4.2×10⁶ / 120 = 35,000 s = 9.7 hours

So a change in the fleet's watts is two-thirds felt after ten hours, if UA is 120. The first hour of it is all the controller can wait for.

5. What a night with every machine on says. 02:00 to 07:00, 18 November: the room stood at 26.00 °C (25.75 to 26.10), the weather averaged 5.7 °C, the fleet 1,280 W, and nothing was changed. By (2):

(P + P0) / UA = 26.00 − 5.7 = 20.3 °C

if P0 were nothing: UA = 1,280 / 20.3 = 63 W/°C (a floor) if UA is 120: P0 = 120 × 20.3 − 1,280 = 1,156 W

One steady night gives one equation in two unknowns. A second night at a different weather gives the second.

6. How cold it can be before the fleet cannot hold 80 °F. The fleet's most is about 1,300 W. From the same night, each watt of (P + P0) is worth 20.3 / (1,280 + P0) degrees, so the coldest weather at which 26.7 °C can be held is

To = 26.7 − 20.3 × (1,300 + P0) / (1,280 + P0) ≈ 6.1 to 6.2 °C (43 °F)

and this hardly depends on P0. Below about 6 °C outside, the room falls short however the fleet is run. That night it went to 3 °C, and the room stood 0.7 °C under its target with every machine working.

7. Energy, and what it bought. 16:44 on the 17th to 08:17 on the 18th, 15.6 hours:

energy into the room: 860 W mean × 15.6 h × 3600 = 48.2 MJ = 13.4 kWh (about $2.28 at 17 ¢/kWh) kept by the room: 4.2 MJ/°C × (26.90 − 26.55) = +1.5 MJ so through the walls: 46.7 MJ, a mean of 834 W, less whatever the other heat added

And the order of preference rests on this, from 25.5 hours on the 16th and 17th, the CPU side's energy for each job finished:

MachineWh a jobCard
columbia3.3no
saskatchewan8.7no
boburner11.3yes
calber18.7yes
whitewolf22.3yes
jaguaribe37.6no
bosporus46.4no

The two Supermicros spend four to five times saskatchewan's energy on a job. Their watts are a model and not a counter's reading.

Part Three: what the first fifteen hours showed

X. The record

Orrery took over at 16:44 on 17 November with the room at 80.1 °F. The stretch before it was a script in a terminal, then the same script in the background; its rules are the law described here.

StretchRoom, °CWeather, °CWhat happened
16:44 to 18:2026.5 to 26.99 to 10Held on target. Connections to the machines were dropping, and lanes stood idle
18:20 to 19:1026.7 to 27.49 to 7The room rose 0.6 °C an hour. The law shed 143 W, then 73 W. A person shed the rest at 18:39. Peak about 27.55 °C (81.6 °F) by the plain mean at 18:44
19:10 to 21:2527.2 to 26.47 to 8Fell back under the ceiling by 19:36; nothing added until the room reached the band's foot
21:25 to 02:0026.4 to 25.67 to 4Heat added a step at a time; the weather fell faster than the steps. A person woke the last machine at 01:39
02:00 to 07:0025.75 to 26.103 to 9Every machine on, nothing left to add. The room stood still, 0.7 °C under its target
07:00 to 08:2026.0 to 26.89 to 11The morning warmed; rising 0.5 °C an hour; calber shed at 08:08

Over the whole of it: the room between 25.60 and 27.40 °C by the controller's own reading (78.1 to 81.3 °F), a mean of 26.28 °C; the weather between 3 and 11 °C; the fleet between 240 and 1,420 W. The controller made 13 changes; a person made 6, and power-cycled calber once more to watch it wake.

XI. Eight faults, and what was done about each

Every one was found by watching it run.

#FaultWhat it didState
1One probe jumps a degree by itself for ten minutesAt 14:03 the mean rose half a degree and a machine was switched off for itCorrected. A probe that moves alone and stands away from its usual place is left out, an hour at most. The log has it left out seven times
2An order to switch a machine off did not count as a change until the machine was downTwo steps a minute apartCorrected
3Only named spares could be wokencalber, switched off by the law, was stranded; bosporus was woken in its placeCorrected. A machine the law switched off is the law's to wake
4Steps were chosen by preference alone, and the pace was forty minutes whatever the budgetAsked for 600 W, it shed 143 W, then 73 W, and the room went through 81 °FCorrected. At the ceiling, the largest step; fifteen minutes when the budget is 400 W or more
5At the ceiling, a probe left out as a spike was not believedA real rise read as 80.8 °F when it was over 81 °FCorrected. For the ceiling the hotter reading is believed
6The machine that carries the thermometers was pausedIts corner cooled, the thermometers read low, and heat was added in another part of the apartment; Paul: "it got hot"Corrected. That machine is left working
7A large budget reached past small steps for a large oneIt woke bosporus, the least efficient machine, over four paused card lanesCorrected. The order of preference is kept whatever the size
8Heat is added only when the room reaches the foot of the bandThe room dipped to 78.1 °F overnight though the fall was visible an hour earlierOpen. It should act on where the room is heading

A ninth is the queue's, not the controller's: pausing a machine's first lane pauses all its lanes. The law now pauses one lane and puts the others back.

XII. What limits it

  • The thermometers are in one corner. Both are on one machine. What is held at 80 °F is that corner. Zone 2 is not read at all.
  • UA is not measured. Calculation 5 gives one equation; the walls flow and the other heat on the Diagram move together with whatever UA is set to.
  • The fleet is too small for a cold night. Calculation 6: below about 6 °C outside it cannot hold 80 °F.
  • Something else heats the apartment in the evening. On the 17th the room rose 0.6 °C an hour at 850 W; the morning before, that rate took 1,260 W.
  • The law has no proof of its own. The ladder, the older law, has sixty checked claims. The hold has two days of running.

Part Four: how the heat is shown

XIII. The techniques, and the reason for each

The Diagram is a process diagram of the kind a plant's control room uses, drawn in the palette of a mathematics film: a dark ground, one colour for each kind of thing.

TechniqueWhat it is hereWhy
NestingThe weather encloses the walls, the walls the apartment, the apartment its two zonesThe geometry is the physics: heat can only go outward through each frame
One colour, one meaningYellow is the fleet's heat, orange the room, blue the weather, violet the heat that is not the fleet's, green the target, red the ceilingA colour is never reused for a second thing, so a glance at a pipe says what is in it
Width is wattsA pipe is a pixel thick for each 70 WThe three flows of the balance can be compared without reading a number
Movement is directionBright marks walk along each pipeWhich way the heat goes is seen, not read
A tank for what is storedThe room's air and thermal mass, with a level and a wordStorage is the term people forget; SOAKING UP and GIVING BACK make the sign of dT/dt a thing that is happening
Hatching for the wallsThe band the heat crosses on its way outThe loss is located where it occurs
Dashes for what is not measuredZone 2's frame, and its empty instrumentA reader must be able to tell a reading from a guess at a glance
Instrument bubblesJI on a power, TI on a temperatureThe convention of process diagrams: a ring is a thing that is read
Said in words, in the warning colour"UA IS A FIGURE IN USE, NOT A MEASUREMENT"; "IMPLIED, not read"The two numbers that rest on a guess say so beside themselves
Thermometers as thermometersGlass, mercury, a scale, the target and the ceiling as marksThe one reading everyone can already read; the two tubes share a scale so the gap between room and weather is a height
Trends beside the numbersHeat in over six hours, the room over threeA number says where it is; a trend says where it is going
Lettering that growsTwice the size on a wide screenThe fonts are bitmaps of one size; at that size on a large display the picture was a stamp in a field
Clocks on every machinetau for the CPU, lag for the drivesThree time scales, a minute, an hour and a day, are why the controller waits

The Hearth panel uses plainer means for a different job: it is where things are changed, so it is words, buttons and one bar. The dangerous button is framed in red and asks twice; the consequence of pressing it is written out above it before it is pressed.

The charts of the report before this one use the same rules on paper: small panels on one time axis, never two scales on one chart, every line named at its end.

Part Five: upkeep

XIV. What it needs from a person

WhenWhatHow
DailyLook at the hold lineIts plan should be under fifteen minutes old and its last words should make sense
DailyRead the day's changes`grep -E 'takesswitchedwoken' QUEUE/hearth/hold.log | tail`
WeeklySave the weather and read the house's fitpython3 tools/hearth-house.py QUEUE --table. The weather service keeps seven days; a week missed is a week lost
WeeklyRead the energypython3 tools/hearth-energy.py QUEUE. The controller refreshes its own copy every twelve hours
After a power cutNothing to setThe mode, the target and the list of what is paused are files and survive. A machine that was off stays off until the room wants it
After a machine is power-cycledAccept itSettings, After a cut: a machine that "came back different" waits for Accept
When a machine is addedProve it wakesSection VI
When a probe is movedSay soIts usual place is learned again within the hour, and the first readings may be left out as a spike

XV. When something is wrong

What you seeWhat it meansWhat to do
"the plan is 20 min old"The passes have stopped: the keeper is down, or the telemetry pull is failingQueue page: is the keeper running? Then python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE step
"NO ROOM PROBE IS FRESH" / "nothing is changed: no room probe is fresh"radbeeper is not running on the probes' machineOn saskatchewan: doas rc-service radbeeper restart. The controller changes nothing while it is blind
The room over 81 °F and risingThe fleet's heat plus something elseLower the target; open a door; press Off on a Supermicro
"SWITCH ON NAME" in the hold's wordsIt is cold, and the only machine left is one it may not wakePress that machine's On, or its power button
"too cold, and nothing is left ... The fleet has no more to give"Every machine is onNothing. See calculation 6
A tile says "tau ?" or "no drive read"The heat page's model did not finish that passIt fills in at the next
Jobs "sent back: host unreachable" every few minutesThe queue's shared connections are being closed. On three occasions this began when the Orrery app was opened and it stopped when the app was closedClose the app when not looking. The cause is not found

XVI. The files

All under QUEUE/hearth/:

FileWhat it holds
state.jsonThe target, the mode, the settings
plan.jsonThe last pass: what both panels draw
hold.jsonWhat the law holds paused, what it switched off, each probe's usual place
hold.logIts words, a line a look
hold.tsvThe room, the weather, the fleet's watts, a line a look
steady.tsvEach two hours the room did not move: the house's loss being measured
machines.jsonEach machine's card address, whether it wakes, how long it took
power.jsonThe last On or Off order for each machine
energy.jsonWatt-hours a job, for the order of preference

XVII. Method

Every figure is from the controller's own files or from the three read-only tools, run on 18 November between 08:00 and 08:30. The two annotated pictures are frames of the program drawn from the live plan at 08:19 and 08:21, with numbered marks added by tools/report/hearth-annotate.py. The calculations were done by hand from the logged values and compared with the logged or drawn result; where they differ in the last digit it is rounding of the slope. Nothing was changed on the fleet for this report.

XVIII. What is not done

  • UA is not measured, and so neither is the other heat.
  • Zone 2 has no thermometer, and zone 1 has them in one corner.
  • The eighth fault, acting on where the room is heading, is open.
  • The hold has no proof script.
  • Steady stretches were counted only inside the target's band until the morning of the 18th, so the five still hours of that night were not written down by the controller; calculation 5 takes them from the log instead.
  • The On and Off buttons have been pressed by a person on the command line and not in the app.
  • Why opening the app closes the queue's connections is not found.

XIX. Added later the same morning: four of the open items closed

Paul, 18 November: "analyze conclusions and action items. Implement the best of your ideas." The sections above stand as they were written at 08:30, and the film was made from them. Between 08:40 and 09:15 four things changed.

Item aboveWhat was done
Why opening the app closes the queue's connections (sections XV, XVIII)Found, and corrected. An ssh server allows ten sessions on one connection and refuses the eleventh: "no more sessions" in its log, exit 255 at the Mac, which the queue reads as the host being unreachable. The queue's jobs and every housekeeping tool shared one connection a machine; with the app open and asking, the count went past ten. whitewolf's log has "no more sessions" in the hours of 14 November's incident, in the hours the app was open on the 17th and 18th, and in no others. The housekeeping tools (machines, storage, growth, boots, power and six more) now share a second connection of their own, so a job is never the one refused
Fault 8: acting on where the room is heading (section XI)Corrected. If the room is moving 0.15 °C an hour or more and will be out of the band within three quarters of an hour, the step is taken now
The hold has no proof (sections XII, XVIII)It has one. python3 tools/hearth-hold-check.py drives the law through 30 claims on a made-up fleet and ends PASSED. Writing it found two more faults, both corrected: "at the ceiling" began 0.15 °C under it, which left a tenth of a degree in which the order of preference applied at all (so the first machine shed on the morning of the 18th was calber, a card machine); and a size limit of 250 W kept calber, at 313 W, from being the first machine woken
UA is not measuredBegun. Standing still is now the room not moving, wherever it stands, and each stretch is set against the weather the room has felt (its mean over the hours before, the newest counting most), not the weather of that minute. The night's two stretches, taken at the minute, said 58 and 68 W a degree; set against the weather felt, 68 and 67. python3 tools/hearth.py QUEUE steady lists them; with four stretches standing 3 °C apart the line through them gives UA and the other heat, and the hold takes that UA for its budget by itself

Still open: zone 2 has no thermometer; the thermometers of zone 1 are in one corner; the two Supermicros' watts are a model; the fleet cannot hold 80 °F below about 6 °C outside.
